name: Codex (cloud agent)
official_status_notes: Cloud-hosted Codex agent for GitHub tasks (issue -> PR) with parallel sessions and sandboxes; separate from the open-source Codex CLI (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Included with ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Team/Enterprise classes; usage-limited.
strengths: Parallel sessions, sandboxes, GitHub integration, reliable handoff via PR.

name: AutoCodeRover
official_status_notes: Academic autonomous program improvement system (Apache-2.0); maintained under the AutoCodeRoverSG org (README contact routes via SonarSource). Resolves GitHub issues via a search+patch pipeline (verified Sep 2026).
weaknesses: Academic tooling; not a polished product.

name: Agentless
official_status_notes: The previously recorded repository no longer resolves (404, verified Sep 2026) â€” verify the project's current location before relying on this entry.
weaknesses: Not a realtime coding tool for interactive use.

name: Devin
official_status_notes: Fully autonomous AI engineer (cloud); Cognition also acquired Windsurf (2025-07) and ships Devin in Windsurf. Subscription-based; verify pricing.
best_for: Long-running autonomous tasks with review-based handoff.
strengths: Full autonomy, parallel sessions, GitHub/PR integration, IDE companion.
weaknesses: Price; closed source; best learned after mastering simpler agents.

name: Jules
official_status_notes: Google's async GitHub coding agent: clones repo to cloud VM, plans with Gemini, proposes PR (verified site Sep 2026): free 15 tasks/day; Pro 100/day; Ultra 300/day.
pricing_summary: Free tier with daily limits; Pro/Ultra tiers with more tasks.
best_for: Delegating well-scoped GitHub tasks to a PR-producing cloud agent.
strengths: Free tier, async cloud execution, clear plan-then-PR flow.
weaknesses: Cloud-only (code leaves your machine); task limits.

name: Factory Droid
official_status_notes: Factory's autonomous software engineer product ('Droid'). Enterprise agent-native development focus; verify current availability/pricing.
best_for: Enterprise engineering orgs running autonomous agents at scale.
strengths: Autonomous, cloud, covers the SDLC loop.
weaknesses: Enterprise focus; costly; not a student tool.

name: Sweep
official_status_notes: GitHub-integrated junior-developer agent (issue to PR). Verify whether the product/company is still operating in 2026.
pricing_summary: Not verified â€” check official documentation.
weaknesses: Status uncertain; superseded by newer cloud agents.

name: AutoGPT
official_status_notes: Open platform for building and running AI agents; managed platform is paid, self-hosting is free (own infra + model keys). Licensing: classic/ is MIT; autogpt_platform/ is Polyform Shield (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Self-host: no license fee (you pay infra + model keys); managed platform: paid plans.
best_for: Building and running goal-driven agent workflows â€” self-hosted or managed.
strengths: Large community; many integrations; self-host path stays free.
weaknesses: Platform licensing is not fully open; heavier infrastructure than a CLI agent; output quality depends on your models.
hardware_requirements: Self-hosting wants Docker and spare RAM; tight on 8 GB machines.

name: Devika
official_status_notes: Open-source (MIT) 'AI software engineer' (early Devin alternative). README (verified Sep 2026): very early/experimental stage; a successor ('Opcode') is announced â€” verify current state before relying on it.
pricing_summary: Free, open source; model API keys at your own cost.
best_for: Studying an early open-source autonomous software-engineer design.
strengths: Open source; local-model (Ollama) configuration; plan â†’ code loop.
weaknesses: Experimental; unfinished features; unclear long-term maintenance.
hardware_requirements: Runs a local server + web UI; models can be cloud or Ollama.

name: MetaGPT
official_status_notes: Multi-agent framework ('software company' roles: PM, architect, engineer); MIT; CLI (`metagpt "..."`) and Python library; LLM config supports OpenAI/Azure/Ollama/Groq etc.; the commercial MGX product is separate (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source; model API costs depend on your provider.
best_for: Multi-agent 'software company' simulations and one-prompt project scaffolding with a strong research lineage.
strengths: MIT; active research; role-based multi-agent pipelines; local-model config.
weaknesses: Research-grade output quality; heavier than single-agent CLIs.
hardware_requirements: Light client; models via API or Ollama.

name: gpt-engineer
official_status_notes: GitHub repo archived 2026-04-22 (read-only). README: the precursor to lovable.dev; recommends Aider for a maintained CLI (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source (archived); model API costs at your own cost.
best_for: Historical study: the OG prompt-to-codegen CLI experiment that seeded Lovable.
strengths: Simple CLI (`gpte`); benchmark harness; open source.
weaknesses: Archived â€” not maintained; README points to Aider/Lovable for active paths.

name: CodeRabbit
official_status_notes: Proprietary AI code-review service for GitHub/GitLab pull requests (plus IDE and CLI review surfaces); free trial and a free plan for open source (verify eligibility on the official page) (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free trial; paid plans per seat; free plan for open-source projects â€” verify on the official pricing page.
best_for: Automated first-pass review on every PR with committable suggestions.
strengths: PR-native; learns from repo history; IDE and CLI review options.
weaknesses: Closed source; review noise and limits vary by plan; enterprise pricing.

name: Greptile
official_status_notes: Proprietary AI code reviewer built on a codebase graph index; Starter is free for one developer (unlimited repos, 50 credits/mo) and Pro is $30/seat/mo per the official FAQ; self-hosted option for enterprise; MCP integration and a CLI (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Starter: free for 1 developer (50 credits/mo); Pro: $30/seat/mo â€” verify current pricing on the official page.
best_for: Teams that want context-aware PR review that learns repo conventions.
strengths: Codebase-graph context; custom rules; MCP and CLI; self-host for enterprise.
weaknesses: Closed source; credit-based pricing can be unpredictable on large PRs.
